# Install novada-mcp

### mcp-registry

```
# Registered with the official MCP Registry (remotes-only entry) — see distribution/registry-publish.md for the one-time `mcp-publisher publish` step.
```

- **Audience:** Infrastructure, not user-facing — makes novada-mcp discoverable by registry-aware clients; nobody runs an install command against this file directly.
- **Auth:** N/A at this layer — server.json only DESCRIBES the server's own runtime auth (Bearer header documented informationally); the server's actual auth is OAuth 2.1 at the hosted endpoint, same as every other row below.
- **Publish / what the owner must still do:** `mcp-publisher publish` (reads server.json from CWD) — OWNER-GATED, see distribution/registry-publish.md. The file itself is regenerated on every `npm run build` by gen-server-json.mjs.

### claude-code-plugin

```
/plugin marketplace add NovadaLabs/novada-mcp
/plugin install novada-mcp
```

- **Audience:** to-B — a developer runs `/plugin install` in their own Claude Code.
- **Auth:** OAuth 2.1 (hosted endpoint's Authorization Server, auto-triggered on first connect). Manual NOVADA_API_KEY header alternative documented in INSTALL.md for setups that cannot complete a browser OAuth flow.
- **Publish / what the owner must still do:** git push to NovadaLabs/novada-mcp main — Claude Code reads plugin.json live from the repo; there is no separate publish step.

### claude-code-marketplace

```
/plugin marketplace add NovadaLabs/novada-mcp
```

- **Audience:** to-B — same audience as claude-code-plugin; this row is the marketplace LISTING entry, not a second install path.
- **Auth:** Same as claude-code-plugin — this row only lists the plugin, it does not change how the installed plugin authenticates.
- **Publish / what the owner must still do:** git push to NovadaLabs/novada-mcp main.

### smithery

```
npx -y @smithery/cli install novada-mcp --client claude
```

- **Audience:** to-B — a developer runs the Smithery CLI against their own client.
- **Auth:** Local stdio package — auth is whatever NOVADA_API_KEY the user supplies directly to the npm package; no OAuth involved at this layer.
- **Publish / what the owner must still do:** Smithery re-reads smithery.yaml from the GitHub repo on each deploy trigger; no separate publish step beyond pushing to main.

### glama

```
# Installed via `npx novada-mcp` — Glama lists the npm package; there is no separate Glama CLI install step.
```

- **Audience:** to-B, discovery only — Glama is a directory; the actual install command is `npx novada-mcp`, same auth as the smithery row.
- **Auth:** N/A — glama.json carries no auth configuration of its own.
- **Publish / what the owner must still do:** Glama re-crawls the npm registry + GitHub repo periodically; glama.json only configures maintainers, so there is nothing to publish from this repo.

### gemini-cli

```
gemini extensions install https://github.com/NovadaLabs/novada-mcp
```

- **Audience:** to-B — a developer adds the extension to their own Gemini CLI.
- **Auth:** OAuth-first — VERIFIED from gemini-cli source this round (see this row's notes): a header-less httpUrl server triggers automatic OAuth discovery on a 401. Manual NOVADA_API_KEY + settings[].envVar + ${VAR} header-templating alternative documented in INSTALL.md (requires the experimental.extensionConfig flag).
- **Publish / what the owner must still do:** Fully automatic, decentralized crawler — no submission form, no PR. Google re-reads the tagged public repo's root continuously once the `gemini-cli-extension` GitHub topic is set (owner-gated, one-time, see distribution/github-topics.md). Real-world caveat, UNVERIFIED-THIRD-PARTY (community bug reports, not an official doc): some repos meeting every documented requirement still fail to appear in the gallery for weeks — treat 'passes the daily crawl' as probabilistic.

### antigravity-plugin

```
agy plugin install https://github.com/NovadaLabs/novada-mcp/tree/main/distribution/plugins/antigravity
```

- **Audience:** to-B — a developer runs `agy plugin install` against their own Antigravity IDE/app.
- **Auth:** OAuth-first via Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) — automatic, no headers/settings needed. No ${VAR} templating mechanism exists for this channel (CONFIRMED absent in antigravity.google/docs/mcp) — unlike Gemini CLI, there is no manual API-key alternative; OAuth is the only shipped auth path.
- **Publish / what the owner must still do:** No self-serve publish/listing API or PR path exists for the Antigravity MARKETPLACE — listing is gated behind a manual interest-form request (antigravity.google/docs/marketplace). DIRECT install via `agy plugin install <github-url>/tree/<ref>/<subpath>` (this row's install_snippet) bypasses the marketplace entirely and needs no registration step.

### openai-codex-plugin

```
mkdir -p ~/.codex/plugins/novada-mcp
cp -R distribution/plugins/openai/. ~/.codex/plugins/novada-mcp/
# Restart Codex (or run `codex`) and enable "novada-mcp" via /plugins. This manual ~/.codex/plugins/<name>
# copy is OpenAI's own documented personal-install shortcut (developers.openai.com/codex/plugins/build,
# re-verified live 2026-10-15, brief-F R8) around authoring a .agents/plugins/marketplace.json entry.
# For the shared ChatGPT+Codex directory listing (broader distribution, not local/dev): submit via
# https://platform.openai.com/plugins (owner-gated manual review, see distribution/INSTALL.md).
```

- **Audience:** to-B for the LOCAL/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json install path; to-C-REACHING for the shared ChatGPT+Codex Agent Plugins directory submission (platform.openai.com/plugins) — any ChatGPT consumer can discover/enable a published app, not only developers. This materially raises OpenAI's review bar (see publish_mechanism and INSTALL.md).
- **Auth:** OAuth 2.1 is MANDATORY for the shared-directory submission path — CONFIRMED, API-key headers are explicitly rejected by OpenAI's review policy. DCR-based, no headers/oauth block needed in .mcp.json, matching novada-mcp's hosted Authorization Server. For the LOCAL marketplace.json path, a user may separately hand-configure Codex's own ~/.codex/config.toml with a literal bearer-token env-var reference themselves — that is the user's OWN local config, never part of this shipped plugin bundle.
- **Publish / what the owner must still do:** Two independent mechanisms, not to be conflated: (1) LOCAL/team plugin install via `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` + a local/git plugin source — no portal, no review, works today. (2) The shared ChatGPT+Codex 'Agent Plugins' directory (platform.openai.com/plugins) — web-portal ZIP upload -> automated tool scan -> 'Submit for review', OAuth 2.1 mandatory for any authenticated data access, EU-data-residency OpenAI projects explicitly blocked from submitting (both CONFIRMED, developers.openai.com/plugins/build/auth and .../deploy/app-review).
